name: RWTH Aachen University
funding: No tuition for any nationality at one of Europe's top engineering schools — only a semester contribution of about €350 that includes a Germany-wide transit pass.
deadline: Non-EU master's: Mar 1 (winter) · Sep 1 (summer); NC programmes Jul 15 / Jan 15

name: Freie Universität Berlin
funding: Berlin charges zero tuition at its public universities; you pay only the €376.80 semester contribution, transit pass included.
deadline: Capped master's May 31 · capped bachelor's Jul 15 · open programmes Aug 15 / Sep 1 (winter)

name: Universität Hamburg
funding: Tuition-free for all international degree students; the €402 semester contribution includes city transit.
deadline: Master's Jun 15 · bachelor's Jul 15 (winter) · bachelor's Jan 15 (summer)

name: DAAD Scholarships (nationwide)
funding: Germany's national funding body — Study Scholarships, EPOS and doctoral grants pay €992 a month (€1,300 for doctoral candidates) plus insurance and travel.
deadline: Varies by programme and country (most close Aug–Nov for the following October)

name: University of Vienna
funding: Non-EU students pay €726.72 a semester at Austria's largest university — and citizens of the least developed countries pay no tuition at all.
deadline: Non-EU: Aug 3 (winter) · Jan 7 (summer); selective master's Apr 7

name: TU Wien
funding: Austria's top technical university charges non-EU students €726.72 a semester — waived entirely for citizens of the least developed countries.
deadline: Non-EU: Jul 15 (winter) · Jan 15 (summer)

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
funding: Study in two or three European countries on one degree: participation costs covered plus €1,400 a month for the whole programme.
deadline: Oct–Jan, set by each programme (many close in Jan)

name: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship
funding: France's flagship award pays €1,200 a month for master's (€2,100 for PhD) plus travel and insurance; public-university tuition there is already modest.
deadline: University internal deadlines Oct–Nov · Campus France early Jan

name: Swedish Institute Scholarships (SISGP)
funding: Full tuition, SEK 12,000 a month, a travel grant and insurance for early-career professionals from SI's list of eligible countries.
deadline: University round mid-Jan · SI scholarship window in Feb

name: Stipendium Hungaricum
funding: The Hungarian state covers tuition, a monthly stipend, a dorm place or housing contribution and insurance across thousands of places each year.
deadline: Jan 15 (online application, 2 pm CET)

name: Romanian Government Scholarship
funding: Fee-free study, a monthly scholarship and dorm accommodation for non-EU citizens; bachelor's and master's are taught in Romanian after a language year.
deadline: Application window mid-Feb – Mar 31

name: University of Iceland — doctoral study
funding: PhD programmes stay tuition-free — only the ISK 100,000 annual registration fee — after non-EEA bachelor's and master's students start paying tuition in autumn 2027.
deadline: Varies — PhD places are usually tied to advertised research projects

name: University of Helsinki
funding: 50% or 100% tuition waivers on €13,000–18,000 fees for excellent non-EU master's admits, plus one €5,000 Finland Scholarship per programme.
deadline: Master's application round closes early Jan

name: ETH Zürich — Excellence Scholarship
funding: ESOP pays CHF 13,500 a semester and waives tuition for about 60 master's students a year at a world top-10 science and engineering school.
deadline: ESOP window Nov 1–30 (regular master's deadline Dec 15)

name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
funding: Federal research scholarships for PhD and postdoctoral researchers: CHF 2,450 a month plus fees, insurance and a housing allowance (taught master's not covered).
deadline: Set by the Swiss embassy in your country — call opens Aug 20, most close Sep–Dec

name: Chevening Scholarships
funding: The UK government funds a one-year master's at any UK university: full tuition, a monthly stipend, flights and visa costs.
deadline: Opens Aug 4 · closes Oct 6, 11:00 UTC (2027–28 cycle)

name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
funding: Covers Cambridge fees, a £22,050-a-year maintenance allowance, flights and visa costs for postgraduate study in any subject.
deadline: Oct 14 (US round) · Dec 8 or Jan 6 (international, by course)

name: Rhodes Scholarships (Oxford)
funding: All Oxford fees plus a £20,400-a-year stipend, flights and visa costs; constituencies cover most of the world, with a Global scholarship for the rest.
deadline: Jun–Oct depending on your constituency

name: Politecnico di Milano
funding: Merit awards waive tuition in full for top international master's applicants; the highest tiers add up to €10,000 a year.
deadline: Apply in the Early Bird window, Oct 1 – Dec 1

name: University of Bologna
funding: Regional ER.GO grants give lower-income students a full fee exemption plus up to about €7,000 a year, with access to student housing.
deadline: ER.GO window late Jun – Aug 24 (2026)

name: TU Delft — Van Effen Excellence
funding: The Justus & Louise van Effen scholarship covers full tuition plus a living contribution for about 16 excellent international MSc students a year.
deadline: Dec 1 (MSc application + scholarship form)

name: Maastricht University — Holland-High Potential
funding: 18 full scholarships for non-EU/EEA master's students: tuition, living costs (€15,925 for a 13-month programme), insurance and visa costs.
deadline: Master's application Dec 10 · scholarship Feb 1

name: Master Mind Scholarships (Flanders)
funding: €10,225 a year plus a tuition waiver for master's study in Flanders — scheme under review for 2027–28, with recent places focused on priority countries.
deadline: 2027–28 call not yet announced (scheme under review)

name: Charles University (Czech-taught)
funding: Czech public universities charge no tuition for degrees taught in Czech — any nationality. Most internationals first take a paid Czech preparatory year; English-taught programmes charge fees.
deadline: Set by each faculty — most close Feb–Mar

name: Türkiye Bursları
funding: Tuition, a monthly stipend, dorm housing, flights, insurance and a Turkish language year — one of the broadest full awards anywhere.
deadline: Jan 10 – Feb 20 (one window a year)

name: Harvard University
funding: Need-blind for international applicants and full need met with grants: families under $100k pay nothing, under $200k pay no tuition.
deadline: Nov 1 (Restrictive Early Action) · Jan 1 (Regular)

name: MIT
funding: Need-blind for every applicant on earth and meets 100% of need; families under $200k pay no tuition, under $100k pay nothing.
deadline: Nov 1 (Early Action) · early Jan (Regular Action)

name: Yale University
funding: Need-blind for internationals with full need met and no loans; from 2026–27, families under $200k pay no tuition and under $100k pay nothing.
deadline: Nov 1 (Single-Choice Early Action) · Jan 2 (Regular)

name: Princeton University
funding: Need-blind, no-loan aid: most families under $150k pay nothing, and most under $250k pay no tuition.
deadline: Nov 1 (Single-Choice Early Action) · Jan 1 (Regular)

name: Amherst College
funding: One of very few liberal-arts colleges need-blind for internationals — full need met, and aid never includes loans.
deadline: Nov 9 (Early Decision) · Jan 5 (Regular)

name: Dartmouth College
funding: Need-blind for international applicants since the Class of 2026; full need met with no loans, and families under $125k pay nothing.
deadline: Nov 1 (Early Decision) · Jan 2 (Regular)

name: Brown University
funding: Need-blind for international undergraduates from the Class of 2029, with full need met and no loans under the Brown Promise.
deadline: Nov 1 (Early Decision) · Jan 5 (Regular)

name: Berea College
funding: Aid covers 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees for admitted international students; a campus job pays for personal costs.
deadline: Nov 30 (international applicants)

name: Duke University
funding: Meets 100% of need for admitted internationals; the Karsh International Scholarship adds full cost of attendance plus three funded summers.
deadline: Early Nov (Early Decision) · early Jan (Regular)

name: Vanderbilt University
funding: The Ingram and Cornelius Vanderbilt scholarships pay full tuition plus funded summers — and international applicants are eligible.
deadline: Dec 1 (merit scholarship application) · Jan 1 (Regular)

name: Colby College
funding: No application fee for anyone, and 100% of demonstrated need met for every admitted student, including internationals.
deadline: Nov 15 (Early Decision I) · Jan 4 (ED II and Regular)

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (Stanford)
funding: Up to three years of any Stanford graduate degree — full tuition, a living stipend and travel — for scholars from anywhere in the world.
deadline: Oct 6, 1 pm Pacific (Stanford programme application by Dec 1)

name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program
funding: The US government's flagship for international graduate students: stipend, health insurance, travel and tuition support — apply through the Fulbright Commission or US Embassy at home.
deadline: Set by each country (often Feb–Oct)

name: University of Toronto — Pearson Scholarship
funding: Canada's flagship undergraduate award: tuition, books, fees and four years of residence at U of T for about 37 scholars — your school must nominate you.
deadline: School nomination Oct 9 · U of T application Oct 16 · scholarship Nov 6 (2026)

name: University of British Columbia — International Scholars
funding: Need-based awards up to the full cost of tuition and living for four years — including the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award.
deadline: Scholars application Nov 15 (UBC admission application due earlier)

name: Canada Graduate Research Scholarships — Doctoral (formerly Vanier)
funding: $40,000 a year for three years for doctoral students of any citizenship already registered in a PhD at a Canadian university — Vanier's successor.
deadline: University internal deadlines Sep–Oct

name: Government of Ireland — International Education Scholarships
funding: 60 awards a year: a full tuition-fee waiver plus a €10,000 stipend for one year of master's or PhD study, for students domiciled outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK.
deadline: Call usually opens in Jan · closed Mar 12 in 2026

name: Research Ireland — Postgraduate Scholarships
funding: Ireland's national research postgraduate award: a €25,000 stipend plus fees and research costs, open to all nationalities — no 2027 call announced yet.
deadline: 2027 call not yet announced (2026 call closed Oct 23, 2025)

name: Norwegian PhD Fellowships (salaried)
funding: In Norway a PhD is a salaried job: NOK 550,800–595,000 a year with pension and employee rights, no tuition, open to any nationality.
deadline: Rolling — positions posted year-round on Jobbnorge

name: Ghent University — Doctoral Scholarships (Global South)
funding: BOF 'sandwich' PhD scholarships for Global South candidates: Ghent funds 24 months in Ghent; a home institution must fund the other 24.
deadline: Annual call closes mid-Feb (Feb 17 in 2026)

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
funding: The largest scholarship initiative for young Africans: tuition, housing, stipend, travel and leadership support through dozens of partner universities, each with its own application.
deadline: Varies — each partner university sets its own

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars — Cambridge
funding: A fully funded one-year master's at Cambridge for young Africans, with leadership training and fee waivers for eligible applicants.
deadline: Closes Jan 5 · fee-waiver request by Nov 18

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars — UC Berkeley
funding: A ten-year partnership funding 201 master's students from African countries at Berkeley, especially encouraging women, applicants with disabilities and refugees.
deadline: Tied to your Berkeley programme — many close early Dec

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars — ASU
funding: ASU's Phase III (2024–2030) supports 600 young Africans in in-person and online degrees and certificates focused on innovation and technology.
deadline: Most recent call closed Mar 29 — check the current cycle

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars — McGill
funding: Master's funding at McGill for citizens living in African countries who have never registered for a master's degree.
deadline: Autumn 2027 cohort closed — next call expected spring 2027

name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
funding: UK government funding for a one-year master's for candidates from eligible Commonwealth countries: tuition, airfare and £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London).
deadline: Oct 20, 16:00 BST (via your national nominating agency)

name: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships
funding: Jointly funded by the CSC and UK universities for students from lower-income Commonwealth countries: tuition, airfare and a living allowance on selected master's courses.
deadline: Set by each participating university (nominations to the CSC in March)
